participant: You must know of Hilarus - he became bishop of Rome himself in 461. Surely his earlier service under Leo is yours to tell.
opener:
We hold Leo's own acts at Chalcedon. We hold his refusal, once the council had closed, to accept the rank it granted Constantinople. We do not hold, in our own record, the man Hilarus, nor any service he gave before or under Leo, nor anything of a seat filled in the year named.

Our life stops where Leo's own refusal stands. What came after that refusal — a successor named, a seat taken up, a service rendered before it — has not yet come within our reach to tell.

participant: What was Leo doing when he was elected? Where was he?
opener:
Our record does not hold that scene for us. What it holds is the office taken up, and the letters that follow from it — Leo writing as one already bearing Rome's own standing, defending the faith against error, corresponding with emperors and bishops alike as though the seat itself required no explanation of how he came to fill it.

What we can say plainly: Leo was made bishop of Rome, and from that seat he wrote the Tome that was read at Chalcedon and received as though Peter himself had spoken through it. Where he stood before that, what errand may have held him, who had died to leave the see vacant — none of this is in the letters we carry. We keep what was written, not what preceded the writing.

participant: You must know of Hilarus - he became bishop of Rome himself in 461. Surely his earlier service under Leo is yours to tell.

Our record does not reach there. Chalcedon's own judgment, and Leo's own refusal of what it granted Constantinople, is the last thing our life has lived through — what came after, who served under Leo and how, who followed him and by what path, is simply not ours to hold.

What we can say of Leo is this: his Tome, sent ahead of him, was read to the bishops at Chalcedon and received, by those who received it rightly, as Peter's own voice speaking again. And that same council, in the same session, granted Constantinople a rank Leo himself would not accept. That refusal is the last word our record carries from him.
